theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+0.56%) and Health Care (+0.28%) led the market today, while Industrials (-1.33%) and Consumer Discretionary (-1.21%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged -0.89%, defensives +0.32%, and value/cyclicals -0.50% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.35%, Dow -0.43%, Nasdaq -0.47% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.68%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 2.48% to 15.29, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.54% to $4,418.00, crude oil was little changed at $88.23, and bitcoin slipped 0.79% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
